lines.line: Narrator's dad works for <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>>? Don't tell viewers.
That's rule five of the BBC rulebook.
Ofcom, twenty twenty five: a British Broadcasting Corporation Gaza film was materially misleading.
The narrator's father? A <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> government official.
Rule three. Hospital explodes? Blame Israel first.
BBC, live: hard to see what else this could be, other than an Israeli air strike.
U.S., British and French intelligence: likely a rocket from Gaza.
Rule nine. <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> are militants. Never terrorists.
BBC's John Simpson: calling someone a terrorist means taking sides.
Britain banned <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> as terrorists in twenty twenty one.
Rule two. Army brings doctors? Report: targeting doctors.
Al Shifa, twenty twenty three. BBC: the army is targeting medical teams.
Not true. The army brought medics. BBC apologised.
White House: <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> used Al Shifa as a command and control node.
The BBC does issue corrections. Judge it by the record.
Send this to someone who still trusts rule five.

transcript.heard: Narrator's dad works for Hamas, don't tell viewers. That's Rule 5 of the BBC rule book, Ofcom 2025. A British Broadcasting Corporation Gaza film was materially misleading. The narrator's father, a Hamas government official. Rule 3. Hospital explodes, blame Israel first. BBC Live. Hard to see what else this could be, other than an Israeli airstrike. US, British and French intelligence. Likely a rocket from Gaza. B.C. Wrong to Speculate. Rule 9. Hamas are militants. Never terrorists. BBC's John Simpson. Calling someone a terrorist means taking sides. Britain banned Hamas as terrorists in 2021. Rule 2. Army brings doctors? Report. Targeting doctors. Al-Shifa, 2023. BBC. The army is targeting medical teams. It's not true. The army brought medics. BBC apologized. White House. Hamas used al-Shifa as a command and control node. The BBC does issue corrections. Judge it by the record. Send this to someone who still trusts Rule 5.
